option_relations.rationale: Primary central nervous system lymphoma (PCNSL) is a distinct entity from Intravascular Large B-Cell Lymphoma with CNS involvement. While both involve the CNS, the primary location and pathogenesis differ.

The option 'Intravascular large B-cell lymphoma' is clinically equivalent to the leaf 'Intravascular Large B-Cell Lymphoma with CNS involvement'. The CNS involvement is a common and often defining feature in the clinical presentation of intravascular large B-cell lymphoma, especially when it presents with neurological symptoms.

Secondary CNS involvement by systemic diffuse large B-cell lymphoma implies a systemic primary lymphoma with subsequent CNS metastasis, which is different from intravascular large B-cell lymphoma that primarily affects the CNS vasculature without a clear systemic primary in many cases.

Lymphomatosis cerebri variant of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) is a specific pattern of CNS involvement by DLBCL, characterized by diffuse infiltration of the brain parenchyma. While it involves DLBCL, it is a distinct entity from intravascular large B-cell lymphoma.
